# Case 1: simple 3x3 symmetric distances, k=1
{"k":1,"dist":[[0,1,2],[1,0,3],[2,3,0]]}
@ Each node connects to its single nearest neighbor; weights use 1/(1+d)
{"weights":[[0,0.5,0],[0.5,0,0],[0.3333333,0,0]]}

# Case 2: same 3x3 matrix, k=2
{"k":2,"dist":[[0,1,2],[1,0,3],[2,3,0]]}
@ Each node connects to its two nearest neighbors
{"weights":[[0,0.5,0.3333333],[0.5,0,0.25],[0.3333333,0.25,0]]}

# Case 3: 4x4 rectangle distances, k=1
{"k":1,"dist":[[0,5,3,4],[5,0,4,3],[3,4,0,5],[4,3,5,0]]}
@ Each node connects to its single closest neighbor (distance=3 → weight=0.25)
{"weights":[[0,0,0.25,0],[0,0,0,0.25],[0.25,0,0,0],[0,0.25,0,0]]}

# Case 4: 4x4 rectangle distances, k=2
{"k":2,"dist":[[0,5,3,4],[5,0,4,3],[3,4,0,5],[4,3,5,0]]}
@ Each node connects to its two closest neighbors (distances 3 and 4)
{"weights":[[0,0,0.25,0.2],[0,0,0.2,0.25],[0.25,0.2,0,0],[0.2,0.25,0,0]]}

# Case 5: k larger than N-1 (clamped inside topKNeighbors), N=3
{"k":5,"dist":[[0,1,2],[1,0,3],[2,3,0]]}
@ Effective behavior same as k=2 for N=3
{"weights":[[0,0.5,0.3333333],[0.5,0,0.25],[0.3333333,0.25,0]]}
